title: Implement protective stop coordinator and broker capability-based policy
description:
Build the centralized protective-order manager and a provider-neutral ProtectionPolicy.

In mike_trade/risk/stop_policy.py:
- Define a ProtectionMode enum with FIXED, TRAILING_NATIVE and TRAILING_STEPPED. Define TRAILING_STEPPED now so the policy type is complete, but the coordinator must report it as not yet available until a later phase implements it.
- Define an immutable ProtectionPolicy dataclass with these fields:
  - mode
  - required (bool)
  - order_semantics: STOP_MARKET or STOP_LIMIT, with an optional limit offset
  - fixed reference: CONFIRMED_FILL_PRICE by default, or a configured reference
  - distance: percent, USD, ATR multiple or support level. Validate that exactly one is set for FIXED.
  - native trailing distance: trail_percent or trail_price. Validate that exactly one is set for TRAILING_NATIVE.
  - time_in_force (DAY or GTC)
  - allow_fractional_protection (bool, default False)
  - optional documented_fractional_risk_ack (str)
- Define a BrokerProtectionCapabilities value object. It declares whether the provider supports each of these, and whether each has been paper_proven:
  - stop-market and stop-limit
  - standalone trailing_stop with trail_price or trail_percent
  - fractional protective orders per order type and TIF
  - GTC vs DAY protective TIF
  - linked/bracket/OTO/OCO legs per order type. Linked trailing legs must be representable as unsupported.
- Implement evaluate_policy(policy, capabilities, execution_mode, quantity) -> ProtectionEligibility. It returns ALLOWED, or REJECTED with a reason code. Reason codes:
  - UNSUPPORTED_MODE
  - UNSUPPORTED_ORDER_TYPE
  - FRACTIONAL_NOT_SUPPORTED
  - FRACTIONAL_NOT_PAPER_PROVEN
  - TIF_NOT_SUPPORTED
  - LINKED_TRAILING_UNSUPPORTED
  - STEPPED_NOT_AVAILABLE
- Evaluation must fail closed:
  - In LIVE mode, any fractional, TIF or linked combination that is not paper_proven is REJECTED.
  - Fractional quantity is REJECTED unless allow_fractional_protection is set and a documented risk acknowledgement is present.
- Every eligibility result carries explicit risk notes stating that:
  - a stop trigger price is not a guaranteed execution price or maximum loss
  - stop-limit may not fill
  - DAY TIF expires and leaves an overnight residual

In mike_trade/risk/protection.py:
- Implement ProtectionCoordinator. It is keyed by PositionCycle id and holds a broker-port protocol, injected by dependency injection, plus a clock.
- Methods:
  - check_entry_eligibility(policy, capabilities, mode, intended_qty). A required protection that is not eligible means the entry is rejected before submission.
  - on_confirmed_fill(cycle_id, cumulative_filled_qty, avg_fill_price). Protection starts only after a confirmed positive fill.
  - on_exit_requested(cycle_id, qty, reason). This coordinates discretionary, manual and strategy exits with the active protective order. Cancel the protective order or confirm it is cancelled or filled before releasing exit quantity, or reduce/replace it, so that total working sell quantity never exceeds the confirmed remaining long quantity.
  - on_broker_order_update(...)
  - current_protection(cycle_id)
- The coordinator invariant is at most ONE effective full-position protective sell order per cycle. Any replacement must wait for cancel confirmation of the old order before the new one is submitted, or use a broker-atomic replace.
- The coordinator must operate independently of BUY/SELL strategy cadence, the pause state and the minimum-hold rule. These must never be consulted to delay or skip protection.
- A failed placement or failed coverage after a fill marks the cycle UNPROTECTED_POSITION and raises a fresh-entry block signal (an entry_block_reasons output). It must never be silently swallowed.
- All quantities and prices use Decimal. All timestamps are timezone-aware UTC.
- Keep the broker interaction behind a Protocol; do not import Alpaca-specific code here.

Write tests/unit/test_protection_policy.py with positive and negative cases for policy validation, capability gating, fractional rejection, the single-effective-order invariant and the overlapping-sell prevention.

Before editing, inspect:
- existing mike_trade/risk/ modules from earlier phases (budgets, entry guards, eligibility)
- the domain models for PositionCycle, Order, Fill and Position, and the execution-mode enum (BACKTEST/SHADOW/PAPER/LIVE)
- the broker port/adapter protocols under mike_trade/brokers/
- the clock abstraction
- the Decimal/UTC conventions
Reuse existing types rather than redefining them. Decision budget: if a needed domain type is missing, define a minimal local Protocol in protection.py rather than editing files outside allowed_write_paths.
acceptance_criteria: mike_trade/risk/stop_policy.py defines ProtectionMode with FIXED, TRAILING_NATIVE and TRAILING_STEPPED, plus ProtectionPolicy, BrokerProtectionCapabilities and evaluate_policy.

ProtectionPolicy validation rejects a FIXED policy with zero or multiple distance definitions, and a TRAILING_NATIVE policy with both or neither of trail_price and trail_percent. Each rejection case has a unit test.

evaluate_policy returns REJECTED with a specific reason code in each of these cases, and each case has a unit test: fractional quantity without allow_fractional_protection; fractional or TIF combinations that are not paper_proven in LIVE mode; a linked/bracket/OTO/OCO trailing leg; TRAILING_STEPPED while it is unavailable.
Eligibility results expose risk notes stating that a stop trigger is not a guaranteed execution price or maximum loss, and that DAY TIF leaves an overnight residual.
ProtectionCoordinator never has more than one effective protective sell order per PositionCycle. A test shows that replacement waits for cancel confirmation before a new order is submitted.
on_exit_requested never allows working sell quantity (protective plus exit) to exceed the confirmed remaining long quantity. Tests cover partial fills and manual close.
Protection is triggered only by a confirmed positive fill. A zero or unconfirmed fill creates no protective order (tested).
Protection behaviour does not depend on strategy pause state or minimum hold. A test shows protection is placed while the strategy is paused and during the minimum-hold window.
A placement failure after a fill yields UNPROTECTED_POSITION and an entry block reason (tested).
All money and quantity values are Decimal and all timestamps are timezone-aware UTC. No float is used for price or quantity in the new modules.
tests/unit/test_protection_policy.py passes when run in isolation and makes no network or broker credential access.
forbidden_changes: change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
import Alpaca-specific modules into mike_trade/risk/protection.py or mike_trade/risk/stop_policy.py
create live or paper broker orders or read broker credentials
run broad test suites or backtests
use float for prices, quantities or budgets
